note: Divergences from the vendor that the proxy makes on purpose. Each is data, not an exception in code: it carries the surface it applies to, the exact behavior, and why. A divergence that stops being true fails the same check that a new one does — a stale exemption hides a fixed defect and lets the next regression through. Seed of the manifest described in docs/conformance-suite-design.md §2.

divergences.behavior: The proxy accepts function tools together with a reasoning effort other than 'none' and runs them. The direct API refuses that combination for the gpt-5.6 family with 400 invalid_request_error, param 'reasoning_effort', message "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for <model> in /v1/chat/completions. To use function tools, use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'."
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-30: gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol refuse it, gpt-5.5 accepts it, so the refusal is one model family's limitation on OpenAI's own chat endpoint. The Codex backend behind this proxy runs the combination, and the option rules refuse only what cannot be realized — refusing a request the backend executes would be the violation, not the parity.

divergences.behavior: The proxy accepts `output_config.task_budget` ({type:'tokens', total: >= 20000}) and uses it. The direct API does not know the member and answers 400 `output_config.task_budget: Extra inputs are not permitted` — its `output_config` takes only `format` and `effort`.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-31: the direct API's output_config member set is {format, effort}. `task_budget` is this proxy's own extension over the Claude CLI's task budget, so it is an ADDITION to the surface rather than a difference in shared behaviour. Nothing a direct-API client sends is answered differently; a client that sends it gets the CLI knob it names. Removing it would take a capability away with no parity gain.

divergences.behavior: The proxy answers 400 `model: String should have at least 1 character` for a whitespace-only model name. The direct API treats it as a NAME and answers 404 model-not-found.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-31: `model: '   '` returns 404 on the direct API, the same answer it gives any name it does not know. This proxy runs every model name on its configured backend and so has no name it does not know — it cannot mirror that 404 for one input without mirroring it for all of them, which would break its purpose. It keeps a 400 for the one shape that is plainly a slip rather than dispatching a turn for it.

divergences.behavior: The proxy accepts a replayed item — `reasoning`, a hosted-tool call or its output — without checking its `id`. The direct API answers 404 `Item with id '<id>' not found.` for an id it does not hold, including alongside a valid user turn, and finds the id when the item really came from its own previous response. This entry is about the ID LOOKUP only. What an accepted item then becomes is a separate behaviour and a separate entry: `responses-replayed-hosted-tool-items-are-transcript-records`.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-31. Feeding `output` back as `input` is the documented way to hold a conversation on a surface that stores none, and this proxy stores none either: it has no id table to look one up in. Mirroring the 404 would mean refusing EVERY replayed item, the legitimate ones included, which would break the round trip the surface exists for.

divergences.behavior: What a replayed item BECOMES, once its id has been accepted, depends on the item. A `reasoning` item replays as NOTHING — it is dropped, and a body whose only item is one runs as an empty conversation (`messages: []` reaches the backend). Every OTHER typed item the surface knows, other than the `function_call`/`function_call_output` pair this proxy replays as its own tool history — the hosted-tool calls and outputs a client feeds back to preserve them, `web_search_call` and the rest — replays as a LABELLED TRANSCRIPT RECORD in the turn's own role: the literal `[replayed item]`, then `type: <the item type>`, then the item's own JSON, and that message reaches the backend intact. A `type` the surface does not know is not replayed at all: it is 400 `invalid_value` at `input[<i>]` listing the types it does know. The direct API replays each of these against its own stored copy of the item.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-09-01 at this baseline. The previous wording of `responses-replayed-item-ids-are-not-looked-up` said a hosted-tool item is 'replayed as nothing', which conflated two behaviours and is now false for everything but `reasoning`. These runtimes have no hosted-tool slot to replay such an item INTO, so the honest options are to drop it or to hand the model the record of it; dropping it silently loses conversation the client sent, and writing it as a function tool result made the default transport parse it back into an empty `function_call_output` under an invented id, so the record never reached the model at all. The labelled record is the one form that carries the item's own content through, and nothing parses the label back — so text inside a record cannot forge a tool-result boundary. `reasoning` stays dropped for its own reason: its `summary`, `reasoning_text` and `encrypted_content` have no slot in either runtime, and putting them in a turn told the model its own chain of thought in the user's voice.

divergences.behavior: The proxy accepts a conversation whose last message is an `assistant` turn. `claude-sonnet-5` answers 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.`
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-31. The sentence names the MODEL, and assistant prefill is a capability some Claude models have and others do not. This proxy runs whatever its configured backend runs, so refusing prefill because one model refuses it would refuse a turn the backend can perform — the violation, not the parity. Same shape as `chat-function-tools-with-reasoning-effort`.

divergences.behavior: The proxy accepts a `function` role message and runs the turn: `{"role":"function","name":"f","content":"23C"}` reaches the backend as a TRANSCRIPT turn — the marker line, the function's name, and its output as text — and NOT as a tool result. The role carries a NAME and no call id, so there is no call for a result to answer; it used to arrive as `{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"tool_call"}`, an id this proxy invented, answering a call that appears nowhere in the request (measured on the real transport 2026-09-02, fixed the same day; pinned in `test/tool-history-structure.test.mjs`). The direct API refuses the role OUTRIGHT for `gpt-5.6-terra`, whatever the content — 400 `unsupported_value`, param `messages[2].role`, message "Unsupported value: 'messages[2].role' does not support 'function' with this mode" — with `content: null` and with `content: '23C'` alike. The proxy's own answer for `content: null` is its ordinary missing-content one, at param `messages.[2].content` with no code and the sentence "Invalid value for 'content': expected a string, got null.", so the two sides differ in which fault they report as well as in whether they refuse. `function` remains a value the role enum names on both sides: the proxy's `messages[i].role` enum sentence lists it, and so does the direct API's.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-09-01. The refusal names the MODE — 'does not support ... with this mode' — which puts it in the same class as `chat-function-tools-with-reasoning-effort` and `messages-assistant-prefill-is-not-refused`: a refusal whose sentence names the model or the mode is a capability of that vendor model, not of this surface. The deprecated `function` role is an ordinary transcript turn, and the backends behind this proxy serve it. Refusing a turn the backends CAN serve because one vendor model will not is itself the violation, and this is the safer direction of the two — a client that never sends the role sees no difference, and one that does gets its turn run instead of a 400. Mirroring the refusal would take a working request away for nothing.

divergences.behavior: The direct API's response carries per-hosted-tool token accounting under `tool_usage` — `image_gen` with its own input/output token details, and `web_search.num_requests` — on the one minimal turn captured (P-1), which used neither tool and reported every counter as 0. Whether it appears on every response is not something these bytes show. This proxy reports no `tool_usage` at all.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-29 (P-1, `spec/captures/direct-responses-minimal.json`). These are reporting fields for hosted tools this surface does not run: the proxy's Responses surface has no web search and no image generation of the vendor's kind, so every counter would be a zero asserting that work did not happen rather than a measurement that it did. Matrix §5.5.9 fixed the rule that such a field is not filled by guessing, and the alternative — inventing the counter's semantics for a feature we do not implement — is the failure that rule exists to prevent. A client reading `tool_usage` gets `undefined` instead of a zero; that is the cost, and it is stated here rather than hidden.

divergences.behavior: The direct API's echoed `reasoning` object carries `mode: "standard"` on a request that sends no `reasoning` at all. This proxy echoes `context`, `effort` and `summary`, and no `mode`.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-08-29 (P-1, `spec/captures/direct-responses-minimal.json`). One observed value is not a value space: nothing here has measured what other modes exist, what selects them, or whether the member is even accepted on the request, and no matrix row describes it (`reasoning.context` is R-23, `summary` R-22, `generate_summary` R-24 — `mode` has none). Echoing a constant `standard` would publish a claim about a mode system this proxy has never measured and does not implement. `reasoning.context` went the other way in the same measurement and IS mirrored, because it is a member the request may carry and the echo is mechanical.

divergences.behavior: With `logprobs: true` at `reasoning_effort: none` the direct API answers 200 and fills `choices[].logprobs.content` with one entry per token — the token, its log probability, its UTF-8 bytes, and an empty `top_logprobs` list. This proxy answers 200 and sends no `logprobs` key on the choice at all. A minimal request is not affected: the direct API omits the key there too, which is why the shape comparison for the minimal capture does not read this declaration.
divergences.why: A token's log probability is a property of the decoder that produced it. The local runtimes this proxy drives return finished text over a CLI protocol that carries no per-token probabilities, so there is nothing to report and nothing to derive one from: any number here would be invented. Matrix row 22 already states the acceptance envelope this measures — accepted while the model does not reason, and not applied.

divergences.behavior: The direct API echoes a function tool in a canonical form, filling what the request left out: `description: null`, `output_schema: null`, `strict: true`, and inside `parameters` an `additionalProperties: false` and an empty `required`. This proxy echoes the tool as the request wrote it.
divergences.why: The filled members are not cosmetic — `strict: true` and `additionalProperties: false` say the surface will hold the model's arguments to that schema. This proxy passes tools to a local runtime that enforces neither, so echoing the canonical form would report a guarantee the turn does not carry, and a client that reads its own tool back to learn how it was interpreted would be told the opposite of the truth. Echoing the request's own form is the honest answer available. Filling only the two inert members (`description`, `output_schema`) while omitting the two that mean something would be worse: a partial canonical form reads as the whole one.

divergences.behavior: A request asking for `reasoning.summary: "auto"` is echoed by the direct API as the value it resolved that alias to — `"detailed"` on the one turn measured, at `effort: low`, and that turn carried no reasoning summary in its output either. This proxy echoes `"auto"`, the value the request supplied.
divergences.why: One sample of one alias at one effort is not an alias table. Mirroring it would encode `auto -> detailed` for every effort and every model on the strength of a single turn, and the value is precisely the one a client reads to learn what it will get. Matrix R-22 records the larger fact: this proxy emits no reasoning summaries at all, so resolving the alias would name a summary style for a summary that never arrives. Measuring `auto` at the other efforts is three cheap calls and is listed in the probe plan.

divergences.behavior: The direct API reports five things about how IT ran the turn: which service tier served it, which inference geography it ran in, a breakdown of cache writes by the TTL they were written at, and the thinking tokens the turn spent. This proxy reports none of them. It does report `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` when the runtime behind it gives numbers for them — those are not in this declaration.
divergences.why: Measured 2026-09-10 over the six anthropic captures in `artifacts/direct-api-captures`: `service_tier` is "standard" in all six, `inference_geo` is "global" or "us" following the request, `cache_creation` carries `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` and `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` (0 in all six), and `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` is present in all six. The first four name a mechanism this proxy does not have rather than a number it is failing to pass on: there is no tier system behind a single local runtime, no inference geography to route to, and no cache that distinguishes a five-minute write from a one-hour one. `thinking_tokens` is a DIFFERENT case and is declared here for a different reason — the number exists, the runtime simply does not report it. `claude-code-backend.ts` never populates `reasoningOutputTokens`, so any value emitted here would be a constant. Publishing it as `?? 0` was tried on 2026-09-10 and reverted the same day: a thinking model reporting that it did not think is worse than reporting nothing, which is the judgement `anthropicUsage` already records for the cache counters. Reporting it when it IS measured is `docs/design-task-unmeasured-thinking-tokens.md`.

divergences.behavior: Sent `moderation: {model: "omni-moderation-latest"}`, the direct API answers 200 AND attaches a `moderation` object: `input` and `output`, each a `moderation_results` carrying one `moderation_result` with `flagged`, 13 `categories` booleans, 13 `category_scores` numbers and 13 `category_applied_input_types` arrays — 127 paths. This proxy validates the option exactly as the direct API does (`moderation.model` required, else `missing_required_parameter`), answers 200, and emits no `moderation` key at all.
divergences.why: The local runtimes moderate nothing. Matrix §5.5.9's rule — a reporting field for a feature this proxy does not run is not filled by guessing — applies here HARDER than it does to `tool_usage`, because these are not counters: they are a classifier's verdicts. A `flagged: false` and 26 scores would be this proxy asserting the outcome of a check it never ran, on content it never screened, to a client that asked to have it screened. There is no honest constant. The cost is stated rather than hidden: a client reading `response.moderation` gets `undefined` instead of a verdict, and `docs/api-interface-contract.md` says so. Declared rather than described because matrix row 49 had recorded this in prose since 2026-08-30, which means a build that started emitting a `moderation` block would have agreed with a paragraph instead of failing a gate — the same argument that converted A-28 and A-30 a day earlier.
